settings.question: When should I switch to winter tires in Calgary?
settings.answer: The general rule is when daily temperatures stay consistently below 7°C — usually mid-to-late October in Calgary. Don't wait for the first snowfall: by then every tire shop in the city is booked out two weeks. Plan to install your winter tires by mid-October, and switch back in mid-to-late April when overnight lows stay above 7°C.

settings.question: Are winter tires legally required in Alberta?
settings.answer: Not within Calgary city limits or on Alberta highways. But they ARE required on Highway 93 (the Banff highway) and the Trans-Canada through the mountains during the Oct 1 – Apr 30 winter-tire period. Any tire marked with the 3PMSF (three-peak mountain snowflake) symbol meets the requirement.

settings.question: How long do winter tires last in Calgary?
settings.answer: Most premium winter tires (Michelin X-Ice Snow, Bridgestone Blizzak WS90) last 4 to 6 winter seasons when used only in winter (Nov–Mar) and stored properly the rest of the year. That's roughly 40,000–60,000 km of winter-only use. Running winters year-round destroys them in 18 months — the soft compound wears fast on warm asphalt.

settings.question: Should I get studded snow tires in Calgary?
settings.answer: Only if you regularly meet glare ice — icy gravel back roads, or packed ice that never quite clears on side streets. For most Calgary drivers on plowed routes, a modern studless snow tire like the Blizzak WS90 or X-Ice Snow is quieter, better on wet and bare pavement, and close enough on ice. Full breakdown on the studded tires page.

settings.question: Can I just put winter tires on the front wheels of my front-wheel-drive car?
settings.answer: No. Always install winter tires on all four wheels, even on a FWD car. Mismatched tires create a dangerous handling imbalance — your front end will grip but your rear end will slide out on turns. Every tire manufacturer and Transport Canada is unanimous on this. We won't install two winter tires on a vehicle for this reason.

settings.question: Are snow tires and winter tires the same thing?
settings.answer: Yes. "Snow tires" and "winter tires" are two names for the same product, and you'll hear both in Calgary. What actually matters is the 3PMSF marking — the three-peak mountain snowflake stamped on the sidewall. That symbol means the tire passed a standardised snow-traction test. A tire marked M+S (mud and snow) without the snowflake is not a true winter tire. When you're comparing tires, check the sidewall for that symbol — it is the difference between a real snow tire and an all-season with a winter-sounding name.

settings.question: When should I put snow tires on in Calgary?
settings.answer: Once daytime highs sit consistently below 7°C, which in Calgary is usually mid-to-late October. Seven degrees is the compound threshold, not a snow threshold — winter rubber starts outperforming all-season rubber well before the first snowfall. Waiting for snow means waiting in line with everyone else. Our guide to winter tire timing in Calgary goes through it month by month.

settings.question: When do you take winter tires off in Alberta?
settings.answer: The same 7°C rule, in reverse — usually sometime in April once overnight lows stop dipping back down. There is no rush to beat a date, but there is a cost to leaving them on: winter compound is soft by design, and it wears quickly once the roads warm up. A season of summer driving on winter tires can cost you a whole winter of tread life.

settings.question: Are studded tires legal in Alberta?
settings.answer: Yes, year-round, with no seasonal restriction — unlike British Columbia. Studs bite into glare ice, which is the one surface where studless winter tires give up ground. The trade-off is noise on bare pavement and more wear on dry roads. If you mostly drive plowed city streets, studless is the better tire. See studded tires in Calgary for the full comparison.

settings.question: What's the cheapest way to get winter tires in Calgary?
settings.answer: Buy value-tier 3PMSF tires rather than premium, and mount them on steel rims so you are not paying to dismount and remount every spring and fall. A value set like the General AltiMAX Arctic 12 or Cooper Discoverer True North starts around $130 per tire and is a genuine winter tire, not an all-season in disguise. We sell at wholesale pricing and match any written quote from another Calgary shop on the same model and size. The expensive route is buying premium tires you don't need for the driving you actually do.

settings.question: Do snow tires need their own rims, or can you swap them onto my wheels?
settings.answer: Either works. Swapping tires on your existing wheels means dismounting, remounting and rebalancing twice a year. A second set of steel rims costs more the first year and then makes every changeover a straight wheel swap — faster, cheaper, and easier on the tire beads. If you run TPMS sensors, a second set needs its own sensors or a re-learn each swap; we handle that either way. Ask for a quote on a set with steel rims.

settings.heading: What winter tires actually do in Calgary
settings.intro:
The difference between a winter tire and an all-season is not marketing — it's chemistry. Below 7°C, standard all-season rubber stiffens and loses its ability to deform around road texture. That means less contact patch, less grip, longer stopping distances. By -20°C an all-season is functionally a plastic puck.

A winter tire keeps its softness in deep cold thanks to a high-silica compound. The tread is also cut differently — narrow sipes that act like thousands of tiny biting edges on snow and ice, and channels that evacuate slush before you hydroplane on the slushy side streets across Calgary.

settings.lead: The 3PMSF symbol is the only marking that counts
settings.text: Three peaks and a snowflake, stamped into the sidewall. It certifies the tire passed a snow-traction test. M+S on its own does not — plenty of all-season tires carry M+S and stiffen up badly below 7°C.

settings.lead: Studless is the default, studded is the exception
settings.text: Modern studless snow tires handle packed snow and most ice well, and stay quiet on bare pavement. Studs only pull ahead on glare ice, and cost you noise and dry-road wear the rest of the time.

settings.lead: Compound matters more than tread depth
settings.text: A winter compound stays pliable at -30°C where all-season rubber goes hard. That flexibility is what keeps rubber in contact with road texture, and contact is what produces grip.

settings.lead: Sizes are the same as your all-seasons
settings.text: A snow tire is a direct swap in your existing size. Going narrower is sometimes suggested for deep snow, but for Calgary's plowed streets and packed ice, matching your factory size is the straightforward choice.

settings.heading: Snow tires vs winter tires: what Calgary drivers are actually asking
settings.intro:
People search for snow tires and winter tires as if they are two products. They are not. Both names describe a tire built with a soft cold-weather compound and a tread pattern cut to bite into snow, and both are identified by the same marking.

What actually separates one snow tire from another:
settings.outro: So if you came here searching for snow tires in Calgary, everything on this page applies. Book an install or call (403) 452-4283 with your size.

settings.lead: Swapping on your existing wheels
settings.text: One set of rims. Each changeover means dismounting the old tires, mounting the new ones and rebalancing — twice a year, every year. Cheapest the first autumn, then a recurring cost.

settings.lead: A second set on steel rims
settings.text: Steel rims cost less than alloys and shrug off road salt and curb damage, which is exactly what a Calgary winter throws at them. After the first year, every changeover becomes a straight wheel swap.

settings.lead: Why a swap is easier on the tires
settings.text: Every dismount and remount works the bead. Bolting on a mounted wheel does not touch it, so tires on dedicated rims tend to see out their full service life.

settings.lead: TPMS on a second set
settings.text: A second set of wheels needs its own sensors, or a re-learn at each swap. Either is handled as part of the install — flag which you have when you book.

settings.lead: Storing the off-season set
settings.text: Whichever set is off the car has to live somewhere clean, dry and out of sunlight. Mounted wheels stack flat; loose tires stand upright.

settings.heading: Winter and snow tires on rims: how packages work
settings.intro: The most common question after price is whether to put snow tires on their own rims. Both routes are normal, and the right one depends on how long you plan to keep the tires.
settings.outro: Ask for a quote on a set with steel winter rims in your bolt pattern, or book a seasonal changeover if your tires are already on rims.

settings.lead: Pressure falls about 1–2 PSI for every 5°C
settings.text: A set inflated on a mild October afternoon can be meaningfully low by the first -25°C morning. Underinflated tires wear at the shoulders and cost fuel, and the dashboard light usually arrives later than the problem.

settings.lead: Chinooks swing temperatures 20°C or more in hours
settings.text: That swing moves tire pressure both directions in a single day, which is why a mid-winter pressure check is worth more here than in a steadier climate.

settings.lead: Thaw-freeze builds the black ice
settings.text: Melt in the afternoon, refreeze overnight. It is the mechanism behind the ice that forms on McKnight, Glenmore and 16th Ave, and it is the surface snow tires are built for.

settings.lead: Take them off in spring, around the same 7°C line
settings.text: Usually April in Calgary. Winter compound is soft by design and wears fast once roads warm up — a summer left on winter tires can cost a full season of tread.

settings.lead: Store the off-season set out of the sun
settings.text: Cool, dry, out of direct sunlight. UV and heat age rubber faster than mileage does.
